newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbek deputies approve budget deficit 3-pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek deputies approve budget deficit 3-pct of GDP.

text.p: Uzbekistan's parliament on Friday approved a budget deficit for 1997 of three percent of gross domestic product, a senior deputy in the former Soviet republic said.
Abdurafik Akhadov, chairman of the parliamentary committee for budget, banking and finance, told Reuters revenue was seen at 273 billion sums while spending would total 295 billion sums.
He said the budget figures were not final.
"The budget aims to strengthen the country's social policy," said Akhadov.
Uzbek President Islam Karimov told a news conference on Friday that annual inflation for 1996 in the resource-rich republic was around 60 percent.
He said the government aimed to reduce inflation in 1997 to about 26-27 percent for the year.
The International Monetary Fund last week said it had suspended a loan to Uzbekistan because of concern at the country's foreign exchange controls and its failure to meet inflation targets.
